messages.subject: question about bootstrapLavaan function
parts:
Hi, 

I am a graduate student working with Dr. Savalei at UBC. This is my first time posting questions here! I feel kind of nervous! But nice to meet everyone here!
I am using bootstrapLavaan function for my research on bootstrapping CFI. I noticed that under the "type" argument, we can implement yuan's method of bootstrap. In Yuan, Hayashi and Yanagihara (2007)'s original paper about this bootstrap method, it talks about bootstrapping RMSEA and how to set the population RMSEA to a specific population value. And indeed, bootstrapLavaan provides the option to set population RMSEA to a specific value using the "h0.RMSEA". My question is if we don't specify "h0.RMSEA", how does the function set the population RMSEA value ? And if we are bootstrapping other fit indices (e.g., CFI), how does it implement Yuan's bootstrap method? 

I am sorry if the question is a bit too naive.. I just read Yuan et al (2007)'s paper and I can't say I understand every thing in the paper..

On 07/09/2014 10:59 PM, Cathy Zhang wrote:
> CFI. I noticed that under the "type" argument, we can implement yuan's
> method of bootstrap. In Yuan, Hayashi and Yanagihara (2007)'s original
> paper about this bootstrap method, it talks about bootstrapping RMSEA
> and how to set the population RMSEA to a specific population value. And
> indeed, bootstrapLavaan provides the option to set population RMSEA to a
> specific value using the "h0.RMSEA". My question is if we don't specify

I'm not sure. This was coded by Ed Merkle
(http://psychology.missouri.edu/merklee), so you may wish to contact him
for more details. But in the source code, so can see this:

# Calculate tauhat_1, middle p. 267.
# Yuan et al note that tauhat_1 could be negative;
# if so, we need to let S.a = Sigmahat. (see middle p 275)
ifelse(length(h0.rmsea)==0,
tau.hat <- (ghat - df)/(n-1), # middle p 267
tau.hat <- df*(h0.rmsea^2)) # middle p 273

so if h0.rmsea is not provided, 'tau.hat' is computed as (ghat -
df)/(n-1), while if you do provide h0.rmsea, it is computed as
df*(h0.rmsea^2))

The page numbers refer to the 2007 paper. Hopefully this helps.

Yves.
